Or paste x, y, z into the x field — it splits automatically.

H01 is a ~1 mm³ sample of human temporal cortex (Shapson-Coe et al., Science 2024, CC BY). Cell types are the dataset's own published classification; soma positions come from joining that classification to the cell_bodies segmentation.

Cortical layer is sampled from H01's own layers volume at each soma centroid. It agrees with the classification's #L1…#WM tags on 94.8 % of cells and, where the two differ, they are always exactly one layer apart — so a “border” badge means the soma sits on that boundary, not that either source is wrong. For the 520 cells the volume does not cover, and for any coordinate outside the cell table, the layer is estimated from fitted geometry (96.0 % accurate against the volume, never off by more than one layer).

Two caveats from the join. spiny-stellate (190 cells) is 62.6 % in L5 rather than L4 by the layer volume and has the largest median soma of any type — treat it as uncertain. And 1,468 c3 segments contain more than one soma, so a segment ID is not always one cell.
